newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo looks abroad for highway investments.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo looks abroad for highway investments.

text.p: Sao Paulo state officials will be in Washington, D.C., on Monday seeking foreign investment for a project to expand the state's major highways, the Transporation Secretariat said.
The state government will present its plan to grant concessions for road work at a seminar called the "International Road Federation" in Washington.

Under the plan, the government would grant a 20-year concession to private investors to manage, operate and expand Anchieta and Imigrantes highways, which link the capital of Sao Paulo to the port of Santos 40 miles (70 km) to the east. Santos is the largest port in the Southern Hemisphere.
The deal involves $600 million in investment, the statement said.

In addition, Sao Paulo state will offer 20-year concessions for the Castello Branco and Raposo Tavares highways, which link the capital with many industrial, agricultural and technological cities in the interior of the state.
These projects are expected to need about $1.3 billion in private investment.
Investments in all of the projects are expected to be recovered after eight years based on an estimated profitability of 18 percent annually, the statement said.
